facts.text: Stoddard was a glass‑making hub between 1840‑1873, employing 800 people and producing amber Stoddard bottles prized by collectors.
The town’s historic two‑story building once housed Nathan Morse’s shoe shop, a milliner, grocery, library, and now the Stoddard Historical Society.
Colonel Sampson Stoddard, after whom the town is named, never lived there; the area was first granted in 1752 as “Monadnock Number 7.”.
Stoddard’s abundant forests supplied the high‑temperature furnaces needed to melt sand into glass, with local sand noted for its fine quality.
The town’s first schoolhouse appeared in 1792, and the first post office opened in 1822 with Isaac Duncan as postmaster.
In 1774, the settlement of 24 residents was incorporated as Stoddard, honoring Colonel Stoddard, after earlier being called “Limerick.”.
